title: Born 1913; listening outside Copasetic and Economy halls
summary: Born March 3, 1913, one of thirteen children. As a kid he hung around the dance halls grabbing the drummer's drum and watching him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, what year were you born? The exact date of your birth, I'd like to give.
In 1913. The third day of March, 1913.
So you're younger than most of the guys that played the old New Orleans style.

Yes, but just like I said, right around that vicinity where I was born, the Copperhead Hall was not too far from me, which is, say, one, two blocks and a half from where I was staying at. And the Economy Hall was four blocks from where I was staying at. Well, when they'd have those dances like that, well, I used to go around, we kids would get around and listen to music. And the first thing I'd do is grab the drummer's drum when they played it. The first one or two numbers on the street, I'd grab the drummer's drum. I wanted to bring it upstairs from him and bring it in the hall. I'd get up there, plow up, and sometime I'd stay up there and stay over my time and listen to them playing. And all my mind was on that drummer, watching that drummer, what he's doing, how he plays. Nobody had a chance to get a set of drums because my parents, we had thirteen of us. My father couldn't afford to buy me those set of drums. They set vinyl, it's not those guys until I just guess it was just a minute to learn how to play, that was all.
Well, would they come down on the banquet or would they be on the porch or what?
